text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Crown Prince Hassan and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak discuss Middle East security during talks in Alexandria; the prince praises the Egyptian initiative to salvage the peace process and efforts to lift collective Israeli punishment against Palestinians.

- Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah says the gap is still large between the Israeli and Palestinian positions but expresses hope on signs of slight relaxation in Israeli punitive measures against Palestinians after easing the closure of border crossings.
- King Hussein calls for joint efforts to support the peace process and the resumption of stalled Israeli-Palestinian negotiations.

- Encouraging signs of progress arising from active Jordanian diplomacy to defuse tensions; the crown prince and Egypt's Mubarak discuss in Alexandria reviving the peace process. Jordanian and Egyptian foreign ministers warn of the dangers of the crisis in peace-making on regional stability.
- The decision by the left-centrist Mustaqbal (Future) party to boycott the coming parliamentary elections next November reverberates within the opposition ranks.
- Government proposals to merge the municipal affairs ministry with the interior ministry.
- Government plans to set up an office to welcome foreign investors at its main international airport; part of an investment promotion drive to attract outside capital to the country.
